findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Spell out trigger_likelihood's maintainability-lane meaning for a coverage/contract finding (parallel to the prod_impact re-scope), so the ×0.75 rare-damping in the moderate lane has a well-defined trigger — or drop the trigger_likelihood term from the moderate-lane formula if reach is already fully keyed by prod_impact.

verify prompt L70-71 (as-written): 'trigger_likelihood ... how often the PRODUCTION consequence actually triggers ... Leave "common" when unsure' — a pure coverage/contract finding has no production consequence, so the honest verifier answer stays the 'common' default
findings.finding: Approach step 3's moderate-maint-lane damping uses trigger_likelihood=rare as a ×0.75 multiplier, but step 2b only re-scopes prod_impact concretely for maint findings; trigger_likelihood's maint-lane meaning is left unspecified. Its existing documented meaning ('how often the PRODUCTION consequence triggers') has no natural reading for a coverage/contract finding, so verifiers will keep the 'common' default and the ×0.75 rare-damping will essentially never fire — silently defeating that half of the moderate-lane user-reach keying.
findings.location: Approach step 2b + step 3 (moderate consequence lane); code-review-verify.md L70-72 + verify_models.py trigger_likelihood field
scenarios: A moderate maint finding (contract_drift / reachable_path_without_automated_coverage) on a genuinely rarely-reached path: the verifier leaves trigger_likelihood='common' because there is no production consequence to rate, so the intended ×0.75 damping never applies and a low-reach finding scores the same as a high-reach one.
findings.suggested_fix: In step 2b and both field descriptions, give trigger_likelihood a concrete maint-lane reading (e.g. 'for a coverage/contract finding, trigger_likelihood = how often the un-covered/contract-violating path is actually exercised'), and confirm the corpus crosstab supports verifiers answering it that way; otherwise remove '× 0.75 when trigger_likelihood=rare' and let prod_impact alone key user-reach.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the step 2(b) re-scope to give trigger_likelihood a concrete maintainability-lane meaning in both code-review-verify.md and verify_models.py (e.g. for a coverage/contract finding, how often the guarded path is actually exercised), so the v4 moderate-lane ×0.75 rare damper reads a value the verifier is told how to set.
evidence: Plan step 2(b): 're-scope the prod_impact / trigger_likelihood field descriptions ... amend to state they also key the maintainability lane's user-reach damping (for a coverage/contract finding, prod_impact = user-facing reach of the guarded path)' — the parenthetical restatement is given ONLY for prod_impact, not trigger_likelihood.
Plan step 3 moderate lane: '× 0.75 when trigger_likelihood=rare — the user-reach keying' — the scorer consumes this enum value.
code-review-verify.md:70 'trigger_likelihood (common|sometimes|rare) — how often the PRODUCTION consequence actually triggers in practice' — the sole definition is production-scoped.

The maint moderate lane uses a DIFFERENT mapping (rare=0.75) than the prod lane (rare=0.25, verify_models.py:402-404), so a verifier judging a coverage finding has no basis to choose 'rare' vs 'common'.
findings.finding: The Pass-3 v4 moderate-maintainability-lane damping keys on trigger_likelihood=rare (×0.75), but the plan re-scopes only prod_impact with a concrete maint-context meaning ('user-facing reach of the guarded path') and leaves trigger_likelihood's maint-context meaning undefined for the verifier — the existing prompt ties it strictly to 'how often the PRODUCTION consequence actually triggers,' which is undefined for a pure coverage/contract finding that has no production consequence.
findings.location: Approach step 2(b) + step 3 (moderate consequence multiplier); code-review-verify.md line 70-72; verify_models.py line 400-405
scenarios: A tests/coverage finding (prod_impact keyed as user-reach) where the verifier must set trigger_likelihood but the prompt only defines it for a production consequence that this finding does not have — the LLM defaults to 'common' and the ×0.75 rare damper never fires, or fires arbitrarily.
Replay reproducing 163/99 depends on how verifiers set trigger_likelihood for maint findings; an undefined maint-context meaning makes the emitted value non-deterministic across models.
findings.suggested_fix: In step 2(b), amend the trigger_likelihood description in both files to add: 'for a coverage/contract (maintainability-lane) finding, trigger_likelihood = how often the guarded/uncovered path is actually reached in practice (common/sometimes/rare); rare damps the moderate maint lane ×0.75.'
